definitions.explanation: The innermost or furthest part of a space, away from the entrance.

examples.english: It's at the back of the room.

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}の{奥|おく}にトイレがあります。
examples.english: The restroom is at the back of the store.

examples.japanese: もう{少|すこ}し{奥|おく}に{進|すす}んでください。
examples.english: Please go a little further back.

examples.japanese: {森|もり}の{奥|おく}に{湖|みずうみ}がありました。とても{静|しず}かな{場所|ばしょ}でした。
examples.english: There was a lake deep in the forest. It was a very quiet place.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{出|だ}しの{奥|おく}を{探|さが}したら、{昔|むかし}の{写真|しゃしん}が{出|で}てきた。{懐|なつ}かしい{思|おも}い{出|で}がよみがえった。
examples.english: When I searched the back of the drawer, old photos came out. Nostalgic memories came back to me.

notes: {奥|おく} indicates the deep interior or back of a space, opposite to the entrance ({手前|てまえ}). It's used for buildings ({部屋|へや}の{奥|おく} - back of the room), natural spaces ({山|やま}の{奥|おく} - deep in the mountains), and even abstract concepts ({心|こころ}の{奥|おく} - depths of one's heart). {奥|おく}さん (okusan) is also a polite term for someone else's wife.
